text:
alex: Hey team, quick payroll/benefits questions after my first week. 1) I didnt see a deposit in my bank yet  is the first paycheck delayed for new hires? 2) I tried to elect HSA but Workday shows the window closed? 3) How long do I have to add my spouse to dental? Thanks!

Priya (People Ops): Hi @alex welcome! Pay cycles are biweekly on Fridays. New hires have a one-cycle delay if paperwork submitted after cutoff, but payroll can sometimes push an off-cycle payment. @diego can confirm. For HSA: the benefits elections window is 30 days from start date; if you missed it we can submit a late enrollment if you have a qualifying life event or we can try to open a one-time exception.

diego (Payroll): Confirming payroll status for @alex  I see onboarding completed 2 days after your start, so standard first deposit will be next Fri. If you need funds sooner we can do an emergency draw (ACH) but that'll be manual and takes 1-2 business days. DM me bank last 4 if you want that.

alex: Ok thanks. For HSA I thought I had until end of month  I selected plans but Workday still says "no election". Is there a separate HSA provider sign-up?

BenefitsBot: BenefitsBot: Enrollment reminder sent. HSA elections are processed through Workday and require the health plan selection to be complete. If your health plan is pending we cannot finalize HSA. Link: https://redwood.example.com/hr/enroll (automated)

Lily (People Ops): @alex can you screenshot the Workday benefits summary and drop it here? If the health plan is showing as active for the correct plan (starts Day 1) we can trigger a manual HSA enrollment with Fidelity. The HSA vendor needs employee SSN + DOB to open account.

alex: Screenshot attached in thread (img_2026.png). It shows "Health: Active (Effective 04/11)" but HSA still blank. Also question on dental: I need to add spouse; what's the cutoff?

Priya (People Ops): Dental: you have 30 days from your benefits effective date to add dependents for initial enrollment. For adding after that, you'd need a qualifying life event (marriage, birth, loss of other coverage). Send spouse info (name, DOB, SSN if comfortable) via the secure HR form: https://redwood.example.com/hr/forms/dependent-enroll.

diego (Payroll): Reimbursements note: any dependent dental premiums deducted pre-tax will show on next payroll after benefits feed. If you add spouse mid-cycle the premium pro-rates and appears on the following run.

alex: Thanks all  last question: if I pay out-of-pocket for a dental exam before spouse is added, can I submit for reimbursement? How do claims work for dental vs vision?

Lily (People Ops): For out-of-pocket dental: submit the claim to DeltaDental via their portal and attach receipt; if you enroll retroactively within the 30-day window, we can backdate coverage to effective date and route claims to be reprocessed. For vision we handle smaller reimbursements via Expensify under category `Vision Reimbursement`. Dental claims go through the carrier.

alex: Great, that's helpful. I'll DM the screenshot and decide if I want the emergency draw. Appreciate the quick answers! :grinning:

Priya (People Ops): Happy to help! Ping @diego for the draw and @Lily for the dependent form if you want help filling it out. We also have a quick FAQ doc: https://redwood.example.com/hr/new-hire-benefits-faq

diego (Payroll): Payroll note: emergency draw requires manager approval; include reason in DM.

alex: Will do, thanks everyone :)
